story: As a client administrator, I want one back office for settings, add-ons, page widgets, scheduled jobs, system logs, maintenance, products and customers, so that staff run the shop day to day.
As a catalogue manager, I want to change details or status of many products at once and archive products in bulk, so that catalogue work at scale is fast.
As a client administrator, I want to suspend and reactivate customer accounts and to process deletion requests, so that problem accounts and privacy requests are handled.

Technical enabler. As a member of the platform team, I want one register of every nopCommerce service override and global action filter the product installs, checked at start, so that two plugins never silently replace the same core service.
As a client administrator, I want to design a business process as steps with branches and parallel paths, so that processes change by configuration instead of new code.
As a client administrator, I want to build processes from ready-made steps: approval, notification, document creation, payment release and a call to another system, so that common steps are reused.
As a client administrator, I want to test a process with sample data before publishing it, so that I see where it would block before it goes live.
As a client administrator, I want processes to have versions so that running cases finish on the version they started with, so that changes never break cases in progress.
As an auditor, I want to replay how a past case moved through the steps, so that disputes and audits can be answered.
As an operations manager, I want internal approval stages, the shipping workflow and the fulfilment processes to run as configured workflows, so that our processes follow our own stages.
As an e-government service administrator, I want each service catalogue entry to use a configured workflow, so that each service follows its own process.

As a client administrator, I want to write business rules — for example "orders over a set amount need approval" — in a constrained rule language without code, so that rules change without developers.
As a client administrator, I want to start rules from a library of categorised patterns, so that common rules are quick to set up.
As a client administrator, I want to test rules against sample data before activating them, so that I know which inputs pass, which fail and why.
As a client administrator, I want conflicting rules to be detected and a precedence order set, so that the right rule wins.
As an auditor, I want every rule evaluation logged with its inputs, result, rule version and time, so that decisions can be audited later.
As an auditor, I want every change to a rule recorded, so that rule changes are traceable.

Technical enabler. As a member of the platform team, I want to define the types of transaction the platform supports and the information each type needs, so that new ways of trading are set up by configuration.
As an operator, I want to pick the type when I start a transaction and have the fields, workflow and documents adapt, so that each transaction follows its type.
As an operator, I want to combine two types in one transaction, for example a request for quotation followed by a contract, so that multi-stage deals stay one record.
As a member of compliance staff, I want rules for who may see, buy or take part in something, so that programmes reach only eligible customers.
As a member of compliance staff, I want to reserve a quota of a product or programme for a defined group, so that policy categories get their share.
As a member of compliance staff, I want customers screened against sanctions lists where the client's jurisdiction requires it, so that we do not trade with sanctioned parties.
As an approver, I want a queue of the items waiting for me, limited to my role, authority and delegations, so that I see only what I may approve.
As a client administrator, I want approvals with several steps or steps that apply only under conditions, so that approvals follow our chain of authority.
As an approver, I want to approve subject to corrections and have the corrections tracked, so that approval takes effect only when the corrections are done.
As an approver, I want to reject with a reason, and the requester to see the reason and what they can do next, so that rejections are fair and actionable.
As a member of compliance staff, I want high-risk actions such as payout account changes to need approval with an audit trail, so that fraud through account changes is stopped.
As a client administrator, I want to configure product and seller moderation queues and how items are assigned, so that moderation work is shared and controlled.
As a member of operations staff, I want one console where I switch between approval, exception, dispute and audit queues without losing my place, so that I work through queues efficiently.
As a member of operations staff, I want an operational view of orders needing pickup, sorting, dispatch and last-mile delivery actions, so that no order is forgotten at any stage.
As a member of operations staff, I want a personal dashboard of my queues, alerts and figures arranged for my role, so that I see my work at a glance.
As a member of operations staff, I want to save my filters as named views, so that I return to common lists in one click.
As a member of operations staff, I want work I started and did not finish kept across sessions, so that I do not lose partial work.
As an experienced operator, I want keyboard shortcuts for common console actions, so that I work without the mouse.
As a member of operations staff, I want a live count of active users, so that I see current load.
As a field operator, I want the console to work on a tablet or phone, so that I can work away from a desk.
As a client administrator, I want to set which file types and sizes may be uploaded in each place, so that only expected files enter the system.
As a client administrator, I want every upload scanned for viruses before it is stored, so that harmful files never reach the system.
As a member of operations staff, I want failed checks, stuck items and integration errors in one queue ranked by severity and age, so that I fix the worst problems first.
As a member of operations staff, I want structured reason codes and a record of how each exception was fixed, so that fixes are consistent and traceable.
As a member of operations staff, I want to apply the same action to many exceptions at once where it is safe, so that repeated problems are cleared quickly.
As an operations manager, I want exceptions that share a root cause to be grouped, so that the cause is fixed once.
As an operations manager, I want alerts when something needs attention, such as orders stuck too long or service targets missed, with thresholds I set, so that issues are caught early.
As a client administrator, I want a private library of transaction templates derived from the vertical defaults, so that repeat transactions are set up quickly and consistently.
As a client administrator, I want every template version kept with author, time and summary, with rollback, so that changes are traceable and reversible.
As a client administrator, I want a template to inherit from a parent with visible overrides, and to clone a template, so that variants stay consistent with their base.
As a template approver, I want changes to active templates to be approved before use, so that untested changes do not reach transactions.
As a client administrator, I want one workspace to reach branding, wording, workflows, rules, document and notification templates, so that configuration is managed in one place.
As a client administrator, I want to see which templates are used most, which are stale and which have errored transactions, so that I maintain the right templates.
As a client administrator, I want to publish anonymised templates to a shared library and adopt templates others published, so that good templates are reused across clients.
As a member of content staff, I want translations of product, category, manufacturer and attribute texts pre-filled for me to check before saving, so that multi-language content costs less.
As a member of content staff, I want the same pre-fill for topics, blog, news, menus, message templates, vendor content and resource strings, so that all site content can be translated the same way.
As a content manager, I want an optional approval step before AI translations go live, so that high-value texts are checked by a second person.
As a member of catalogue staff or seller, I want a product description written from the name, keywords and tone I give, so that listings are written faster.
As a member of catalogue staff, I want meta title, keywords and description generated for products and other pages, so that search listings improve with less effort.
As a seller, I want a suggested price based on comparable products, so that I price competitively.
As a member of catalogue staff, I want attribute values that look wrong flagged for me, so that listing data is reliable.
As a seller without professional photos, I want extra product images generated from the description, so that my listing looks complete.
As a shopper, I want answers to common questions in the website chat and on WhatsApp at any hour, so that I get help at once.
As a shopper, I want to ask the assistant for the status of my order, so that I do not have to wait for an agent.
As a shopper, I want to be handed to a support agent when the assistant cannot help or when I ask, so that I always reach a person if I need one.
As a client administrator, I want to set the assistant's channels, knowledge sources, languages and hand-off rules, so that it answers only what we approve.
As a member of support staff, I want to see the questions the assistant could not answer, so that we improve the approved responses.
As a support agent, I want a draft reply to a ticket based on similar resolved tickets and the knowledge base, so that I answer faster.
As a member of client staff, I want a summary of a long document with its key dates, requirements and obligations, so that I understand it quickly.
As a member of compliance staff, I want text extracted from scanned or photographed documents, so that documents become searchable and processable.
As a member of compliance staff, I want a check of whether an identity document looks genuine, so that fraudulent documents are caught.
As a member of fraud staff, I want each transaction scored by a trained model for fraud risk, so that patterns that rules miss are caught.
As a shopper, I want product suggestions that fit what I look at and buy, so that I find relevant products faster.
As a stock planner, I want a forecast of demand by category, region and time, so that I plan stock better.
As a member of quality staff, I want product photos checked for defects, so that quality control scales.
As a member of legal or sales staff, I want a first draft of a contract or letter from a template and the details I enter, so that documents are prepared faster.
As a shopper or citizen, I want to be told whenever AI is used to answer me or to make content I see, so that I know what I am dealing with.
As a shopper or citizen affected by an AI answer or decision, I want an explanation of how an AI answer or decision was reached, so that I can trust or question it.
As a shopper or citizen, I want to opt out of AI and reach a person where appropriate, so that I am not forced to use AI.
As a client administrator, I want a register of where AI is used and monitoring for unfair bias, so that we use AI responsibly and can show it.

As a member of catalogue staff, I want to maintain a category tree with names in each language, web addresses, pictures and display order, so that products are organised the way customers look for them.
As a client administrator, I want to limit a category to certain customer groups or shops, so that each audience sees its own categories.
As a shopper, I want to browse products by category and subcategory, so that I find products easily.

As a member of catalogue staff, I want to create and edit a product with name, descriptions, SKU, barcode, price, weight, size, pictures and published state, so that every product has complete, consistent information.
As a seller, I want to create and manage my own listings with the mandatory fields title, description, price, stock and images, so that I can sell through the platform once approved.
As a seller, I want to record weight and dimensions for each product, so that logistics can price and plan delivery.
As a client administrator, I want to set which file types and sizes can be uploaded as product images and documents, checked by the server, so that bad or oversized files never reach the shop.

Technical enabler. As a developer of another product module (INV, SRC, SEL, CAT-022), I want one IProductService override, hosted by the core product master record CAT-002, into which my module plugs as a provider, so that the product service is overridden once and every rule runs on every path.
As a member of catalogue staff, I want product codes created automatically from a pattern the client sets, so that codes are unique and consistent without typing them.
As a member of catalogue staff, I want product options such as pack size and descriptive details such as grade, origin or fragile, in each language, so that customers can compare and filter products.
As a seller, I want to record fragility and handling notes on my products, so that logistics handles them correctly.
As a client administrator, I want to decide for each category which attributes and fields must be filled in before a product can be published, so that product information is complete and consistent.
As a seller, I want the system to check my listing for missing fields and image quality before I submit it for approval, so that my listing is not returned for avoidable reasons.
As a member of catalogue staff, I want changes to category attributes and required fields to go through an approval, so that the taxonomy changes under control.

As a member of catalogue staff, I want one product to have versions such as 250 g, 500 g and 1 kg, each with its own code, price, stock and picture, so that customers choose the exact version they want.
As a seller, I want to create a bundle or kit of several of my products and set the bundle price, so that I can sell gift packs and combined offers.
As a shopper, I want to see what is in a bundle before buying it, so that I know what I get.
As a member of catalogue staff, I want to copy an existing product with its settings and pictures, so that I add similar products quickly.
As a seller, I want to save a frequently used set-up as a named listing template and start new listings from it, so that I do not re-enter the same values.
As a member of catalogue staff, I want to add or update many products at once from Excel, CSV or XML files with columns matched by name, so that I save hours of typing.
As a seller, I want to upload my own products in bulk within the limits the client sets, so that I can list my range quickly.
As a member of catalogue staff, I want to export the catalogue to Excel or XML and print a PDF catalogue, so that I can use it offline and in tenders.
As a member of catalogue staff, I want every row of a bulk file checked and all errors listed before anything is saved, so that bad data never goes live.
As a seller, I want a warning before a very large file starts importing, so that I can split it or wait.
As an IT administrator of a partner system, I want to read product and category data through a secure API, so that our systems stay in step without retyping.
As an IT administrator of an ERP, I want to create and update products through the API, so that products are maintained once, in the ERP.
As a member of sales staff, I want different prices for different customer groups and quantities with start and end dates, so that we support retail, dealer, bulk and institutional pricing.
basis: D; Inference from REQ-KTDA-PRJ-002 (retail and bulk business models)

story: As a seller, I want to manage the base price and dated prices of my products, so that my prices stay current.
As a member of sales staff, I want to hide the price of chosen products and show a "request a quote" button instead of "add to cart", so that bulk and negotiated items are sold by quote.
As a business buyer, I want to request a quote from the product page of a call-for-price product, so that I start the negotiation without a cart.
As a member of finance staff, I want each product to carry a tax category or an exemption, so that the right tax is calculated on every sale.
As a member of export staff, I want typed customs fields on each product: HS code, country of origin and duty information, so that international shipping and customs papers are correct.
basis: D; Inference from REQ-KTDA-CUS-002 (international buyers); REQ-KTDA-LEG-001

story: As a seller, I want to fill in the tax and duty fields needed for cross-border shipments where they apply, so that my products can be shipped abroad.
As a shopper, I want several pictures, videos, zoom, 360-degree views and PDF brochures on the product page, so that I can see what I am buying.
As a client administrator, I want image sizes and quality to be configurable and uploads to be validated by the server, so that pages load well and files are safe.
As a shopper, I want product names, descriptions and details in the language I choose, so that I understand what I buy.
As a member of catalogue staff, I want to pre-translate product content by machine and then check it, so that translation is faster.
As a shopper, I want to ask a question on a product page and read earlier answers, so that I can decide with confidence.
As a seller, I want to answer questions on my products, so that common questions are answered once for everyone.
As a member of catalogue staff, I want to moderate questions and answers before they are published, so that nothing harmful is published.
As a member of compliance staff, I want required legal details and certificates with validity dates stored for regulated products, so that we do not sell without valid certification.
As a member of compliance staff, I want a warning before a certificate expires and automatic hiding when it does, so that expired products leave the shop on time.
As a member of compliance staff, I want each product to show its compliance review status, so that we know what is checked.
As a shopper, I want to see where a product comes from — factory, farm or region — and the story behind it, so that I value its origin.
As a member of marketing staff, I want to attach certificates and ownership-chain documents as proof of origin, so that buyers can verify the origin.
As a client administrator, I want to define prohibited categories, items and words and have listings checked automatically, so that illegal or harmful items stay off the shop.
As a shopper, I want to report a suspicious listing from the product page or search results, so that the client can act on it.
As a member of compliance staff, I want to handle takedown requests with the evidence attached, so that we can show what we did and why.
As a member of catalogue staff, I want products to move through stages — draft, in review, approved, published, paused, archived, so that only checked products go live.
As a client administrator, I want approval by one or more approvers in sequence before publishing, so that each listing gets the checks it needs.
As a client administrator, I want to configure moderation queues and the rules that assign listings to them, so that the right people review the right listings.

As a member of seller management staff (through SEL), I want all listings of a seller paused with a reason and resumed only when no reason remains, so that buyers cannot buy from a seller who may not sell.
As a member of catalogue staff, I want every saved version of a product kept, compared and restorable, so that mistakes can be reversed and changes audited.
As a seller, I want my unsaved edits saved automatically as a draft, so that no work is lost.
As a member of catalogue staff, I want to set when a product is available and to allow pre-orders, so that products appear and sell at the right time.
As a member of catalogue staff, I want to withdraw a product with a reason, telling watching customers and handling linked items, so that withdrawal is controlled and traceable.
As a client administrator, I want products not updated for a set number of days flagged, sellers reminded and stale listings paused, so that information and prices stay current.
As a service provider, I want to list a service, not physical goods, with its details, delivery method and the area covered, so that I can sell services in the same shop.
As a shopper, I want clear descriptions of the client's own services, so that I know what I order.
As a shopper, I want to choose an available time slot when I book a service, so that I get a time that suits me.
As a service provider, I want slots never to be overbooked, so that I am not double-booked.
As a citizen (through EGV-003), I want to book a slot at an outlet that handles my e-government service without a cart, so that I can attend the in-person step of my application.
As a service provider (through SVC-003), I want to move, cancel and close bookings through the same booking service, so that capacity stays right after changes.
As a shopper, I want to see where a product or service is on a map, including an area drawn as a shape, so that I know where it is.
As a shopper, I want to write a review and star rating after I bought a product and mark other reviews helpful, so that others can decide better.
As a member of catalogue staff, I want to approve reviews before they appear and to reply to them, so that reviews are fair and answered.
As a seller, I want to mark products that cannot be returned, so that shoppers know before buying and returns follow the policy.
As a shopper, I want the product page to show price, seller, delivery options, estimated delivery time and a returns summary, so that I know what to expect before buying.
As a shopper, I want to see the delivery window and whether pickup is available on the product page, so that I can plan to receive it.
As a shopper, I want the returns policy and how disputes are resolved on the product page and the order page, so that I know my rights.
As an auditor, I want a per-listing record of who viewed or changed what, from which internet address, with old and new values, so that product and price changes are accountable.
As a seller, I want to pay to feature my products in prominent places, so that more buyers see them.
As a member of marketing staff, I want placement rules, schedules and fees that I set, so that placements are fair and earn revenue.
As a member of catalogue staff, I want reports on active listings, categories, out-of-stock rate and listing rejection reasons, so that we know which products work and what to improve.
As a member of marketing staff, I want views, cart and wishlist additions and conversion per product and category, so that we improve the catalogue.
As a member of marketing staff, I want to send product information to marketplaces and comparison sites, so that we reach buyers outside the shop.

As a client administrator, I want to show different product ranges to different customer groups, for example bulk tea to traders and packaged tea to consumers, so that each audience sees what is relevant.
As a member of sales staff, I want the catalogue to support several business models through segments, so that retail and bulk buyers each get their range.
basis: Inference from REQ-KTDA-PRJ-002 (retail and bulk business models)

story: As a member of sales staff, I want minimum, maximum and multiples-of quantities per product, so that orders come in quantities we can supply.
As a business buyer, I want to send an order above the maximum for approval instead of having it refused, so that I can still buy large quantities.
As a seller, I want a step-by-step form that guides me through creating a listing and adapts to the category, so that I create complete listings without training.

As a member of sales staff, I want special price lists for a company or customer, including contract prices with validity dates, that override standard prices, so that key customers get their negotiated prices.
basis: D; Inference from REQ-KTDA-PRJ-002 (contract and bulk business models)

story: As a business buyer, I want to see exactly the products agreed for my company, so that I order only from my agreed range.
As a business buyer, I want to buy by kilogram, chest or carton, with pack sizes and prices based on weight, so that I buy the way bulk tea is traded.
basis: D; Inference from REQ-KTDA-PRJ-002 (bulk business model)

story: As a member of sales staff, I want to set a fixed price in each currency instead of converting from the base currency, so that foreign-currency prices stay stable and round.

Technical enabler. As a developer of another product module (PAY-009 wallet, FIN-003 premium), I want one IOrderTotalCalculationService override owned by CAT-042 into which my module plugs an order-total adjustment, with the adjustment reserved, recorded against the order and kept on admin order edits, so that the order total is changed once, the same way on every path, and the amount used is recorded.
As an approver, I want to review products submitted by sellers and approve, reject or request changes with reasons, so that marketplace listings stay of good quality.
As a seller, I want to see the decision and the reason for each of my listings, so that I can fix and resubmit.
As a client administrator, I want separate queues for seller listings with assignment rules, so that reviews are shared out.
As a shopper, I want to add, change and remove items in a cart and see a mini cart, so that I can collect several items and buy them in one go.
As a registered shopper, I want my cart to be kept between visits and devices, so that I do not lose my selection.
As a shopper, I want to move a cart line to a saved-for-later list and back, so that I can keep items without buying them now.
As a shopper, I want to go through address, delivery, payment and review steps, so that I can complete my purchase.
As a client administrator, I want to choose whether guests may buy without an account or must sign in before payment, so that checkout follows our policy.
As a shopper, I want to see a full order summary before I pay, so that I know exactly what I pay for.
As a shopper, I want a secure checkout where prices and totals cannot be changed from my browser, so that I pay the correct amount.
As a shopper, I want to accept the terms of service before ordering, so that the sale is on agreed terms.
As a shopper, I want the order to be refused if stock or price changed since I added the item, so that I never pay for something that is gone or wrongly priced.
As a member of client staff, I want the payment method and fraud warning signs to be checked again just before the order is placed, so that invalid or risky orders are stopped.

Technical enabler. As a member of the platform team, I want every cart and item check of every module to run in one IShoppingCartService override with provider slots, so that the cart service is overridden once and no module check is lost (decision OVR-REG).

Technical enabler. As a member of the platform team, I want every module that must act inside order placement or inside shipment status actions to plug into one IOrderProcessingService override hosted by this core checkout feature, so that order processing is overridden once and the module rules still apply (decision OVR-REG).
As a shopper, I want to check out and pay once for a cart with items from several sellers, so that buying from many sellers is as simple as buying from one.
As a seller, I want a separate sub-order and task list for my own items, so that I fulfil only my part.
As a member of finance staff, I want order-level amounts to be shared out exactly between the sub-orders, so that totals and settlements reconcile.
As a shopper, I want to choose home delivery or pickup at an outlet for each item, so that I can collect some items and have others delivered.
As a shopper, I want to choose a preferred delivery time window where the service supports it, so that I am at home when the courier comes.
As a shopper, I want to add delivery instructions, so that the courier can find me.
As a client administrator, I want to define delivery windows and their capacity per delivery service and area, so that we only offer windows we can serve.
As a shopper, I want to give a landmark, a map pin and a name for my address, so that couriers can find me where there are no street numbers.
As a client administrator, I want to switch on a post-office box field, including a virtual post box, so that customers can use their box address.
As a courier, I want to see the pin and landmark of the delivery address, so that I find the customer first time.
As a shopper, I want an order reference from the moment checkout starts that stays the same through payment and delivery, so that I can quote one reference everywhere.
As a shopper, I want to resume my checkout after a payment interruption, so that I do not have to start again.
As a member of finance staff, I want pressing pay twice never to create two orders, so that there are no duplicate orders or charges.
As a client administrator, I want to configure the legal notices and confirmations each country requires at each checkout point, so that online sales stay legal in each country.
As a shopper, I want to read and acknowledge the returns and refund policy where it applies before I pay, so that I know my rights.
As a shopper, I want to receive the order confirmation within the time the law requires, so that I have proof of my order in time.
As a client administrator, I want the data-protection and e-commerce notices of the country to be shown at checkout, so that we meet local rules.
As a client administrator, I want to set a minimum order value, so that we avoid unprofitable small orders.
As a client administrator, I want to set a threshold above which delivery or pickup is free, so that customers buy larger baskets.
As a client administrator, I want to block combinations of items that must not be ordered together, so that orders that cannot be fulfilled are not placed.
As a client administrator, I want to make items pickup-only or limit where they can be delivered, so that items go only where they can.
As a client administrator, I want users with account restrictions to be unable to check out, so that suspected fraudsters cannot buy.
As a shopper, I want to choose whether I show an order code or a QR code when I collect my parcel, so that collection is quick and safe.
As a member of outlet staff, I want the code I enter or scan in the LOG-012 collection step to be checked against the code CHK issued, so that only the right person collects the order.
As an agent at an outlet, I want to place an order for a walk-in customer, so that customers who cannot order online are served.
As an agent, I want to record how the customer paid, so that the order and the cash at the outlet match.
As an outlet supervisor, I want to see the orders each agent placed, so that agent work is traceable.
As a shopper, I want to see the expected delivery date or when I can collect, during checkout, so that I know when my order will arrive.
As a business buyer, I want to enter my purchase-order number at checkout, so that our accounts team can match the invoice.

story: As a shopper, I want to add a gift message or special instructions, with a fee where the client charges one, so that my order is handled as I want.
As a business buyer, I want to buy now and pay later against an invoice within my credit limit and terms, so that I can trade as we normally do.
As a member of finance staff, I want to approve credit accounts and set the limit and payment terms, so that credit risk is controlled.
As a member of finance staff, I want orders above the available credit to be refused, so that no one exceeds their limit.
As a business buyer, I want to order by typing product codes and quantities, so that large repeat orders take minutes.
As a business buyer, I want to upload a spreadsheet of codes and quantities, so that I can order from my own lists.
As a business buyer, I want to keep saved order lists and add a whole list to the cart, so that I reorder standard baskets quickly.
As a company buyer, I want orders above my limit to go to an approver in my company before they are placed, so that company spending rules are followed.
As a company approver, I want to approve or reject a colleague's order with a reason, so that I control spending.
As a company administrator, I want to set approval thresholds per company role, so that each person has the right limit.
As a shopper, I want to see a confirmation page and receive a message with my order number, so that I know my order went through.
As a shopper, I want to shop from an Android or iPhone app with the same account, prices and orders as the website, so that I can buy the way I prefer.
As a member of marketing staff, I want to manage the app home page, sliders, product carousels and menus from the admin panel, so that the app shows current offers without a new release.

As a shopper with a low-end phone, I want to install the website on my home screen like an app, so that I reach the shop in one tap.
As a shopper with a weak or costly connection, I want light pages that use little data, so that I can shop on a basic phone or with expensive data.
As a shopper whose connection drops, I want to see an offline page and the pages I already viewed instead of a browser error, so that I can keep reading and know what happened.
As a shopper with a basic phone, I want to dial a short code and check my orders, so that I get updates without a smartphone or internet.
As a shopper with a basic phone, I want to place a simple order from a short menu, so that I can buy without internet.
As a shopper with a basic phone, I want to pay for that order from my mobile-money wallet, so that I can complete the purchase on the same phone.
As a client administrator, I want to set up the menus in each language without code, so that menus match our services.
As a shopper, I want phone menus in my language to check my order, so that I can use the service by voice.
As a shopper who cannot read text messages, I want urgent notifications as automated voice calls, so that I do not miss important updates.
As a client administrator, I want to send text messages through local SMS providers, so that customers on basic phones get updates.

useCaseName: To create an account with my email address and a password
preconditions: Registration type is Standard.
trigger: A visitor submits a unique email address and a password that meets the policy (IAM-003).
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: a visitor submits a unique email address and a password that meets the policy (IAM-003).
2. The system responds: a customer record is created in the Registered role, it is active, the visitor is signed in and the native Customer.WelcomeMessage email is sent (AC-IAM-001-01-01).
3. The customer logs in again later: the saved addresses are offered and the earlier orders are listed in My account (AC-IAM-001-01-03).
exceptionFlow: An account with email E exists: when someone registers with email E, registration is refused with the native message Account.Register.Errors.EmailAlreadyExists and no second record is created (BR-IAM-002) (AC-IAM-001-01-02).

The email, phone or request IP address matches an Active Block entry of the SEL-013 list with scope registration or all: when the registration POST is made (native CustomerController.Register or the IAM mobile registration), no account is created and the SEL-013 block message is shown; the check is the Platform core action filter owned by SEL-013, not an IAM filter (BR-IAM-003) (AC-IAM-001-01-04).
postconditions: A customer record is created in the Registered role, it is active, the visitor is signed in and the native Customer.WelcomeMessage email is sent (AC-IAM-001-01-01).

story: As a shopper, I want to log in with my email address and password, so that I reach my account.

trigger: The correct email and password are entered.

2. The system responds: the customer is signed in and LastLoginDateUtc is set; with MFA the second step of IAM-004 follows (AC-IAM-001-02-01).
exceptionFlow: A registered customer: when a wrong password is entered, login is refused with the native message Account.Login.WrongCredentials and FailedLoginAttempts increases (lockout per IAM-003) (AC-IAM-001-02-02).
postconditions: The customer is signed in and LastLoginDateUtc is set; with MFA the second step of IAM-004 follows (AC-IAM-001-02-01).

postconditions: The guest customer record itself becomes Registered, so its basket and any guest order stay on the account (AC-IAM-001-03-01).

story: As a client administrator, I want to choose how new accounts are activated: at once, after email confirmation, after my approval, or not at all, so that registration follows our policy.

preconditions: Registration type is AdminApproval.
trigger: A visitor registers.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: a visitor registers.
2. The system responds: the account stays inactive until an administrator activates it in the user administration console (IAM-010) (AC-IAM-001-04-02).
exceptionFlow: Registration type is EmailValidation: when a visitor registers, the account stays inactive until the link in the native Customer.EmailValidationMessage email is opened; a login before that is refused with Account.Login.WrongCredentials.NotActive (AC-IAM-001-04-01).
Registration type is Disabled: when a visitor opens the registration page, registration is not possible and the native registration-disabled result page is shown (AC-IAM-001-04-03).
postconditions: The account stays inactive until an administrator activates it in the user administration console (IAM-010) (AC-IAM-001-04-02).

2. The system responds: the account is created without any organisation or company field (AC-IAM-001-05-01).
postconditions: The account is created without any organisation or company field (AC-IAM-001-05-01).

story: As a shopper without an email address, I want to sign up with my mobile number, confirmed by a code sent by SMS, so that I can have an account without email.
useCaseName: To sign up with my mobile number, confirmed by a code sent by SMS
preconditions: Mobile registration is enabled.
trigger: A visitor enters a mobile number.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: a visitor enters a mobile number.

2. The system responds: the number is normalised to international format (BR-IAM-010), checked against existing PhoneIdentity records, and a one-time code is sent through the SMS gateway (IC-IAM-01) with message Iam.Otp.Sent (AC-IAM-002-01-01).

3. The visitor enters the correct code within its validity: a customer record is created in the Registered role with the mobile number as identifier and no email, terms acceptance is recorded (IAM-016) and the visitor is signed in (AC-IAM-002-01-02).
exceptionFlow: The number already belongs to an account: when a visitor tries to register it, no account is created and message Iam.PhoneInUse is shown with the link to log in (AC-IAM-002-01-03).

A code was sent: when the visitor enters a wrong code more times than the configured maximum, the code is invalidated, message Iam.Otp.TooManyAttempts is shown and a new code can be requested only after the resend interval (BR-IAM-012) (AC-IAM-002-01-04).
A code was sent: when the visitor enters it after its validity ended, it is refused with message Iam.Otp.Expired (AC-IAM-002-01-05).
The SMS gateway is unavailable: when a code is requested, message Iam.Otp.Unavailable is shown, no account is created and the failure is logged (AC-IAM-002-01-06).

IAM calls IC-TRK-06 CheckAllowed (recipient = the number, channel SMS, category Security codes, sender IAM) before each IC-IAM-01 SendCode, and TRK answers Blocked (the number is opted out and the client has not marked Security codes mandatory, BR-TRK-031): when a code is requested for that number, no code is sent, message Iam.Otp.Unavailable is shown and the OtpChallenge is not issued; when TRK answers Allowed the code is sent (BR-IAM-150) (AC-IAM-002-01-07).
postconditions: A customer record is created in the Registered role with the mobile number as identifier and no email, terms acceptance is recorded (IAM-016) and the visitor is signed in (AC-IAM-002-01-02).

story: As a shopper, I want to log in with my mobile number and a one-time code, so that I can sign in from any phone.
useCaseName: To log in with my mobile number and a one-time code
preconditions: A customer with a registered mobile number.
trigger: The customer requests a login code and enters it correctly.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the customer requests a login code and enters it correctly.

2. The system responds (native in nopCommerce 5.00): the code is sent through ISmsService to the active ISmsProvider, ValidateCustomerByPhoneAsync sets LastLoginDateUtc and Customer.PhoneSmsVerified, and the customer is signed in (AC-IAM-002-02-04).
3. The customer logs in with email and password, or with mobile number and code: both routes sign in the same customer record (AC-IAM-002-02-02).
4. A customer without an email address makes later requests: the IAM IAuthenticationService override resolves the customer (BR-IAM-011) (AC-IAM-002-02-06).
exceptionFlow: A customer enters an expired code, wrong codes up to OtpSettings.OtpFailedAllowedAttempts, or requests codes beyond the send limit: the native messages PhoneVerification.OtpCode.Error.Expired, Locked or AttemptLimit are shown and no sign-in happens (AC-IAM-002-02-05).
The customer is locked out after wrong passwords, or holds an MFA-required or sensitive role: the IAM filter refuses code-only sign-in (BR-IAM-013) (AC-IAM-002-02-07).
AC-IAM-002-02-01 and AC-IAM-002-02-03 are withdrawn (VER-500): login by code and the code lock are native.
postconditions: The customer is signed in by the native code login; customers without email are resolved by the IAM IAuthenticationService override (BR-IAM-011) (AC-IAM-002-02-04, AC-IAM-002-02-06).

story: As a shopper, I want to recover my account by SMS when I cannot log in, so that I regain access without email.

preconditions: A customer with a registered mobile number cannot log in.

basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the customer chooses recovery by SMS and enters the code correctly.
2. The system responds: the customer can set a new password (where passwords are used) or is signed in, and AUD-IAM-002 is written (AC-IAM-002-03-01).
exceptionFlow: The customer is in a sensitive role (IAM-003): when recovery by SMS is requested, an SMS code alone does not restore access; the extra checks of BR-IAM-020 apply (AC-IAM-002-03-02).
postconditions: The customer can set a new password (where passwords are used) or is signed in, and AUD-IAM-002 is written (AC-IAM-002-03-01).

story: As a client administrator, I want to choose which sign-in factors buyers use (password, SMS code), so that authentication matches our security policy.

basicFlow: 1. Trigger: a buyer opens the login page.

2. The system responds: only the configured factors are offered; "either" is the native OtpSettings.LoginByPhoneEnabled on, "password" is it off, "SMS code" also hides the email and password fields (AC-IAM-002-04-01).
postconditions: Only the configured factors are offered (AC-IAM-002-04-01).

story: As a client administrator, I want to set password length, complexity, reuse and expiry rules, so that weak passwords are not accepted.
useCaseName: To set password length, complexity, reuse and expiry rules
preconditions: CustomerSettings.PasswordLifetime is set and the user role has EnablePasswordLifetime on.
trigger: The password is older than the lifetime.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the password is older than the lifetime.
2. The system responds: every request redirects the user to change the password (native ValidatePasswordAttribute) (AC-IAM-003-01-03).
exceptionFlow: CustomerSettings.PasswordMinLength, PasswordMaxLength and PasswordRequireLowercase / Uppercase / Digit / NonAlphanumeric are set: when a user submits a password that breaks one of them at registration, change or reset, the password is refused with the native validation message for that rule (AC-IAM-003-01-01).
CustomerSettings.UnduplicatedPasswordsNumber is greater than 0: when a user sets one of that many previous passwords, the password is refused (AC-IAM-003-01-02).
postconditions: Every request redirects the user to change the password (native ValidatePasswordAttribute) (AC-IAM-003-01-03).

story: As a client administrator, I want accounts to be locked for a time after too many wrong passwords, so that passwords cannot be guessed.
useCaseName: Accounts to be locked for a time after too many wrong passwords
preconditions: CustomerSettings.FailedPasswordAllowedAttempts is greater than 0.
trigger: A user enters a wrong password that many times.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: a user enters a wrong password that many times.
2. The system responds: CannotLoginUntilDateUtc is set to now plus FailedPasswordLockoutMinutes and further logins return the native LockedOut message until then (AC-IAM-003-02-01).
3. A wrong password is entered for an existing account: the native Customer.FailedLoginAttempt email is sent to the account owner (AC-IAM-003-02-02).
postconditions: CannotLoginUntilDateUtc is set to now plus FailedPasswordLockoutMinutes and further logins return the native LockedOut message until then (AC-IAM-003-02-01).

story: As a shopper, I want to reset my password through a link sent by email, so that I regain access myself.
