preconditions: An active account.
trigger: The owner requests a reset with the account email.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the owner requests a reset with the account email.
2. The system responds: the native Customer.PasswordRecovery email with a one-time link is sent; the link expires after PasswordRecoveryLinkDaysValid days and cannot be used twice (AC-IAM-003-03-01).
3. A password is changed: sessions signed in before the change are signed out at their next request (AC-IAM-003-03-02).
postconditions: Sessions signed in before the change are signed out at their next request (AC-IAM-003-03-02).

story: As a client administrator, I want recovery of sensitive accounts to need extra checks such as security questions or confirmation by a manager, so that stolen email access alone does not give control of a sensitive account.
useCaseName: Recovery of sensitive accounts to need extra checks such as security questions or confirmation by a manager
preconditions: The account holds a role listed as sensitive.
trigger: Password recovery is requested for it.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: password recovery is requested for it.

2. The system responds: no native recovery link is issued (IAM action filter on CustomerController.PasswordRecoverySend [POST]), a recovery request is opened and the same neutral message Iam.RecoveryRequestReceived is shown as for other accounts (BR-IAM-020) (AC-IAM-003-04-01).
3. The user answers all questions correctly: a one-time reset link is issued; a wrong answer counts as a failed attempt (AC-IAM-003-04-02).

4. Another user holding Customers.CustomersCreateEditDelete confirms it: a one-time reset link is issued; the requester cannot confirm their own request; the decision is audited (AUD-IAM-003) (AC-IAM-003-04-03).
postconditions: A one-time reset link is issued; the requester cannot confirm their own request; the decision is audited (AUD-IAM-003) (AC-IAM-003-04-03).

story: As a client administrator, I want staff in sensitive roles to complete a second check at every login, so that an account stays safe if a password is stolen.
useCaseName: Staff in sensitive roles to complete a second check at every login
preconditions: Role R is listed in the MFA-required roles setting.
trigger: A member of R without a configured MFA provider is signed in.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: a member of R without a configured MFA provider is signed in.

2. The system responds: every request is redirected to the native MFA settings page (route MultiFactorAuthenticationSettings) with message Iam.MfaRequired until a provider is configured (BR-IAM-030) (AC-IAM-004-01-01).
3. The correct password is entered: ValidateCustomerAsync returns MultiFactorAuthenticationRequired and the login completes only after the provider verification succeeds (AC-IAM-004-01-02).

4. MultiFactorAuthenticationSettings.ForceMultifactorAuthentication is inspected: it is off, because the native filter would force every holder of Security.EnableMultiFactorAuthentication, including the Registered role; MFA by role is enforced by the IAM filter only (AC-IAM-004-01-03).
5. The member next makes a request: the member must configure a provider again before continuing, and the removal is audited (AUD-IAM-004) (AC-IAM-004-01-04).
postconditions: The member must configure a provider again before continuing, and the removal is audited (AUD-IAM-004) (AC-IAM-004-01-04).

story: As a member of staff, I want to use an authenticator app, an email code, an SMS code or a hardware security key as my second check, so that I can use what I have.
useCaseName: To use an authenticator app, an email code, an SMS code or a hardware security key as my second check
preconditions: The email-code provider is active.
trigger: A user who selected it passes the password step.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: a user who selected it passes the password step.
2. The system responds: a code is sent to the account email and the login completes only with the correct code within its validity (AC-IAM-004-02-01).
3. A user who selected it passes the password step: a code is sent through IC-IAM-01 to the verified mobile number and the login completes only with the correct code (AC-IAM-004-02-02).
4. The user passes the password step: the login completes only after a valid key assertion for that user (AC-IAM-004-02-03).
5. A user selects it: time-based codes from an authenticator app are accepted as the second check (AC-IAM-004-02-04).
postconditions: Time-based codes from an authenticator app are accepted as the second check (AC-IAM-004-02-04).

story: As a buyer, I want to switch on a second login check for my own account and choose the factor, so that my account is better protected.
useCaseName: To switch on a second login check for my own account and choose the factor
preconditions: The buyer holds Security.EnableMultiFactorAuthentication (native default for Registered).
trigger: The buyer opens the MFA page in My account and selects one of the active providers.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the buyer opens the MFA page in My account and selects one of the active providers.
2. The system responds: later logins of that buyer require the selected factor (AC-IAM-004-03-01).
3. The buyer switches MFA off: it is switched off; a member of an MFA-required role cannot switch it off (AC-IAM-004-03-02).
postconditions: It is switched off; a member of an MFA-required role cannot switch it off (AC-IAM-004-03-02).

story: As a member of staff, I want to log in with the work account I already use, so that I need no separate password.
useCaseName: To log in with the work account I already use
preconditions: An OpenID Connect or SAML 2.0 provider plugin (IExternalAuthenticationMethod with IExternalAuthenticationRegistrar) is active.
trigger: A member of staff signs in at the provider.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: a member of staff signs in at the provider.

2. The system responds: the user is matched to the existing customer through ExternalAuthenticationRecord or verified email and signed in; staff accounts are not created by sign-in alone (Proposed) (AC-IAM-005-01-01).
exceptionFlow: The provider returns an error: when the callback is processed, the native external-authentication error flow runs and the error is logged when ExternalAuthenticationSettings.LogErrors is on (AC-IAM-005-01-02).
postconditions: The user is matched to the existing customer through ExternalAuthenticationRecord or verified email and signed in; staff accounts are not created by sign-in alone (Proposed) (AC-IAM-005-01-01).

story: As a client IT administrator, I want accounts to be created and disabled automatically when people join or leave, so that access follows our directory.
useCaseName: Accounts to be created and disabled automatically when people join or leave
preconditions: A provisioning message "deactivate user" arrives from the identity provider.
trigger: It is processed.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: it is processed.
2. The system responds: the customer is set inactive and RequireReLogin is set, so open sessions end (AUD-IAM-008) (AC-IAM-005-02-01).
3. It is processed: the customer is created with the roles mapped from the groups (mapping is configuration) (AC-IAM-005-02-02).
postconditions: The customer is created with the roles mapped from the groups (mapping is configuration) (AC-IAM-005-02-02).

story: As a business buyer, I want to log in with my company identity provider, so that my company controls my access.
useCaseName: To log in with my company identity provider
preconditions: A company account (IAM-022) has its own provider configured.
trigger: A member signs in through it.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: a member signs in through it.
2. The system responds: the member is signed in and linked to that company (AC-IAM-005-03-01).
postconditions: The member is signed in and linked to that company (AC-IAM-005-03-01).

story: As a client administrator, I want users to be logged out after a configured time without activity, so that an unattended session cannot be used by someone else.
useCaseName: Users to be logged out after a configured time without activity
preconditions: An idle timeout is set for the user class (staff or buyer).
trigger: No request arrives in a session for that time.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: no request arrives in a session for that time.
2. The system responds: the next request is treated as signed out, the session record becomes Expired and the login page shows message Iam.SessionExpired (AC-IAM-006-01-01).
3. The user keeps making requests: the session stays valid and its last-activity time moves forward with each request (AC-IAM-006-01-02).
4. The idle timeout passes: the session still ends, because the check is made on the server session record, not on the cookie lifetime (BR-IAM-040) (AC-IAM-006-01-03).
postconditions: The next request is treated as signed out, the session record becomes Expired and the login page shows message Iam.SessionExpired (AC-IAM-006-01-01).

story: As a client administrator, I want to limit how many sessions one user can have at once, so that a shared or stolen password is less useful.
useCaseName: To limit how many sessions one user can have at once
preconditions: A concurrent-session limit is set and the user already has that many sessions.
trigger: The user signs in again.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the user signs in again.
2. The system responds: the oldest session is revoked, or the new login is refused with message Iam.SessionLimitReached, as the setting says (AC-IAM-006-02-01).
postconditions: The oldest session is revoked, or the new login is refused with message Iam.SessionLimitReached, as the setting says (AC-IAM-006-02-01).

story: As a security officer, I want to force a user off the system at once, so that I can stop misuse immediately.
useCaseName: To force a user off the system at once
preconditions: The officer ends one session of U.
trigger: The action is confirmed.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the action is confirmed.
2. The system responds: only that session is revoked; other sessions of U continue (AC-IAM-006-03-02).
exceptionFlow: The security officer holds Identity.Core.Sessions.CreateEditDelete: when the officer forces user U off, all session records of U are revoked, Customer.RequireReLogin is set so every open cookie of U is rejected, and AUD-IAM-005 is written (AC-IAM-006-03-01).
postconditions: Only that session is revoked; other sessions of U continue (AC-IAM-006-03-02).

story: As a registered customer or staff user, I want my session to be renewed after a sensitive change, so that an old session cannot be reused.
useCaseName: My session to be renewed after a sensitive change
preconditions: A user changes password, MFA settings or is given a new role.
trigger: The change is saved.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the change is saved.
2. The system responds: the user is signed in again with a new session identifier and the old session record is revoked (AC-IAM-006-04-01).
postconditions: The user is signed in again with a new session identifier and the old session record is revoked (AC-IAM-006-04-01).

story: As a client administrator, I want to create my own roles and give them permissions, so that roles match our organisation without code.
useCaseName: To create my own roles and give them permissions
preconditions: A user holds Customers.CustomerRolesCreateEditDelete and Configuration.ManageACL.
trigger: The user creates a role with a name and system name and ticks permissions for it in the native permission pages (SecurityController.PermissionEditPopup).
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the user creates a role with a name and system name and ticks permissions for it in the native permission pages (SecurityController.PermissionEditPopup).
2. The system responds: members of the new role get exactly those permissions and no others (AC-IAM-007-01-01).
exceptionFlow: A user holds Customers.CustomerRolesCreateEditDelete but not Configuration.ManageACL: when the user saves a role or a permission mapping, the save is denied by the native CheckPermission filter and nothing changes (AC-IAM-007-01-02).
postconditions: Members of the new role get exactly those permissions and no others (AC-IAM-007-01-01).

story: As a client administrator, I want administrative and operational users to have access by role only, so that people see and do only what their job needs.
useCaseName: Administrative and operational users to have access by role only
preconditions: A user whose roles do not include Orders.OrdersView.
trigger: The user opens the admin order list.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the user opens the admin order list.
2. The system responds: access is denied by the native CheckPermission filter (AC-IAM-007-02-01).
exceptionFlow: A role holds only view permissions for an area (5.00 view / create-edit-delete split, unchanged from 4.90): when a member tries to save a change in that area, the save is denied and nothing changes (AC-IAM-007-02-02).
postconditions: Access is denied by the native CheckPermission filter (AC-IAM-007-02-01).

story: As a client administrator, I want to limit which products, categories, manufacturers, topics and menus each role can see, so that restricted items stay with the right buyers.
useCaseName: To limit which products, categories, manufacturers, topics and menus each role can see
preconditions: A product has SubjectToAcl on and only role R is allowed.
trigger: A customer outside R browses or searches.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: a customer outside R browses or searches.
2. The system responds: the product is not shown (AC-IAM-007-03-01).
postconditions: The product is not shown (AC-IAM-007-03-01).

story: As a client administrator, I want the roles that product modules rely on (for example Finance, Risk, Agent) to exist with fixed names, so that module permissions work after installation without manual set-up.
useCaseName: The roles that product modules rely on (for example Finance, Risk, Agent) to exist with fixed names
preconditions: The product plugins are installed.
trigger: The application starts.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the application starts.

2. The system responds: every role of BR-IAM-050 exists with exactly its system name and is listed in the admin role list, including roles that hold only native permissions and roles deleted before (the IAM plugin creates them; PermissionService creates a role only when it installs a new permission) (AC-IAM-007-04-01).
3. The role is saved: the system name is unchanged and the permissions of the modules still apply (AC-IAM-007-04-02).
4. The role pack is applied (PLT-003, IC-PLT-01): the native permission is mapped to that role; the native default mappings of other roles are unchanged (BR-IAM-053) (AC-IAM-007-04-04).
exceptionFlow: A role of BR-IAM-050 is not a native system role (IsSystemRole false, so native code allows changing its system name or deleting it): when an administrator changes its system name or deletes it, the IAM action filter on Admin CustomerRoleController.Edit and Delete [POST] refuses the change with message Iam.ProductRoleProtected and nothing changes (AC-IAM-007-04-03).

An exclusion of BR-IAM-054 exists (for example Vendors never hold Orders.ReturnRequestsView): when a pack or an administrator in SecurityController.PermissionEditPopup maps the excluded permission to that role, the pack fails validation, or the IAM action filter refuses the save with message Iam.PermissionExcluded; nothing changes (AC-IAM-007-04-05).

A role pack lists permission system names: when the pack is applied (PLT-003), every name must exist as a 5.00 permission; an unknown name, for example the 4.70 name ManageProducts or a 4.90 name removed in 5.00 such as ContentManagement.NewsView, is reported as an error and grants nothing (BR-IAM-052) (AC-IAM-007-04-06).
postconditions: Every role of BR-IAM-050 exists with exactly its system name and is listed in the admin role list, including roles that hold only native permissions and roles deleted before (the IAM plugin creates them; PermissionService creates a role only when it installs a new permission) (AC-IAM-007-04-01).

story: As a KTDA administrator, I want several roles per user and one role per stakeholder group, so that KTDA user groups and stakeholders can be modelled when they are confirmed.
basis: REQ-KTDA-PRJ-001; Inference from REQ-KTDA-CUS-001 (stakeholder types undefined, KG-16)
useCaseName: Several roles per user and one role per stakeholder group
preconditions: A user holds roles A and B.
trigger: The user opens a function permitted to B only.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the user opens a function permitted to B only.
2. The system responds: access is granted: effective permissions are the union of the roles (BR-IAM-051) (AC-IAM-007-05-01).
3. An administrator creates one role per type with its permission set: each stakeholder user gets the access of its type (AC-IAM-007-05-02).
postconditions: Each stakeholder user gets the access of its type (AC-IAM-007-05-02).

story: As a client administrator, I want to limit a person's permissions to one store, region, category, value band or time window, so that branches can work independently and safely.
useCaseName: To limit a person's permissions to one store, region, category, value band or time window
preconditions: User U has a scope "store S" on Orders.OrdersView.
trigger: U opens the admin order list.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: U opens the admin order list.
2. The system responds: only orders of store S are listed (admin query filtering, registered core modification L1 §6.3) (AC-IAM-008-01-01).
3. A opens the admin order list or the assisted orders list: only orders whose CHK-013 assisted-order record or pickup point is outlet O are listed (AC-IAM-008-01-06).

4. ADM-006 builds the approval queue of U: ADM-006 reads the limit and the active delegations of U through IC-IAM-06 and lists only items within the limit or delegated to U (BR-ADM-030) (AC-IAM-008-01-07).
exceptionFlow: User U has a scope "store S": when U opens an order of another store by its address, access is denied with message Iam.ScopeDenied and the attempt is audited (AUD-IAM-006) (AC-IAM-008-01-02).
User U has a value-band scope "up to value V" on an approval permission: when U approves an item above V, the approval is refused with message Iam.ScopeDenied (AC-IAM-008-01-03).
User U has a category scope on product editing: when U edits a product outside the category, the save is refused and the product list shows only products in the category (AC-IAM-008-01-04).
User U has a time-window scope: when U uses the permission outside the window, access is denied (AC-IAM-008-01-05).
postconditions: ADM-006 reads the limit and the active delegations of U through IC-IAM-06 and lists only items within the limit or delegated to U (BR-ADM-030) (AC-IAM-008-01-07).

story: As a KTDA administrator, I want to give factory or regional staff access to their own unit only, so that KTDA organisational units can work in one platform.
basis: Inference from REQ-KTDA-PRJ-001 (organisational structures; units not stated, G-ORG)
useCaseName: To give factory or regional staff access to their own unit only
preconditions: A region list is configured and records carry a region.
trigger: User U has a scope "region R".
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: user U has a scope "region R".
2. The system responds: U sees and changes only records of region R (AC-IAM-008-02-01).
postconditions: U sees and changes only records of region R (AC-IAM-008-02-01).

story: As an approver, I want to hand over my approval rights to a colleague for a fixed period, so that work continues while I am away.
useCaseName: To hand over my approval rights to a colleague for a fixed period
preconditions: Approver U delegated the approval permission of an ADM-006 queue to V for a period.
trigger: V opens the approval queue inside the period.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: V opens the approval queue inside the period.
2. The system responds: ADM-006 lists the items of U for V, read through IC-IAM-06 GetApprovalAuthority, and V cannot decide an item that V requested (BR-ADM-030) (AC-IAM-009-01-05).
exceptionFlow: User U holds permission P and P is marked delegable: when U delegates P to user V from a start date to an end date, between those dates the permission check for P succeeds for V (IAM IPermissionService override, BR-IAM-070), and outside them it fails (AC-IAM-009-01-01).
U does not hold P, or P is not delegable: when U tries to delegate P, the delegation is refused with message Iam.DelegationNotAllowed (AC-IAM-009-01-02).
The end date of a delegation passes: when V next uses P, access is denied without any manual step and the delegation becomes Ended (SM-IAM-08) (AC-IAM-009-01-03).
V raised a request that needs approval: when V tries to approve it under a delegation, the approval is refused, because segregation of duties still applies (AC-IAM-009-01-04).
postconditions: ADM-006 lists the items of U for V, read through IC-IAM-06 GetApprovalAuthority, and V cannot decide an item that V requested (BR-ADM-030) (AC-IAM-009-01-05).

story: As an auditor, I want a record of every delegation and of every action taken under it, so that accountability is kept.
useCaseName: A record of every delegation and of every action taken under it
preconditions: V acts under a delegation.
trigger: The action is saved.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the action is saved.
2. The system responds: the audit record (AUD-IAM-007 for the delegation; the audit event of the action itself) names V as actor and U as the person on whose behalf V acted (AC-IAM-009-02-01).
3. The change happens: AUD-IAM-007 is written with delegator, delegate, permission and dates (AC-IAM-009-02-02).
postconditions: AUD-IAM-007 is written with delegator, delegate, permission and dates (AC-IAM-009-02-02).

story: As a user administrator, I want to find users and view their details, so that I can help customers quickly.
useCaseName: To find users and view their details
preconditions: A user holds Customers.CustomersView.
trigger: The user searches by email, name, phone, company, role, registration date or last activity.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the user searches by email, name, phone, company, role, registration date or last activity.
2. The system responds: matching customers are listed and each record can be opened (native admin customer list) (AC-IAM-010-01-01).
postconditions: Matching customers are listed and each record can be opened (native admin customer list) (AC-IAM-010-01-01).

story: As a user administrator, I want to activate and deactivate accounts, so that I can stop or restore access without deleting data.
useCaseName: To activate and deactivate accounts
preconditions: A user holds Customers.CustomersCreateEditDelete.
trigger: The user clears the Active flag of customer C.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the user clears the Active flag of customer C.
2. The system responds: C cannot log in (native NotActive result), open sessions of C end at their next request, and AUD-IAM-008 is written (AC-IAM-010-02-01).
3. Staff set Active again: C can log in again and AUD-IAM-008 is written (AC-IAM-010-02-02).
postconditions: C can log in again and AUD-IAM-008 is written (AC-IAM-010-02-02).

story: As a user administrator, I want to see the shop as the customer sees it, with a record kept, so that I can reproduce problems.
useCaseName: To see the shop as the customer sees it, with a record kept
preconditions: A member of Administrators holds Customers.CustomersImpersonation.
trigger: The user starts impersonation of an active customer.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the user starts impersonation of an active customer.

2. The system responds: the IAM impersonation filter allows it (BR-IAM-130), the storefront is shown as that customer and the native activity Impersonation.Started is written for both people (AC-IAM-010-03-01).
exceptionFlow: A user holds Customers.CustomersImpersonation, is not in Administrators, and no registered rule provider (IAM-026 agent rule, CRM-015 account-manager rule) allows the request: when the user posts the impersonation action, the IAM impersonation filter refuses it with message Iam.ImpersonationNotAllowed (or the refusing provider message), no impersonation starts and AUD-IAM-019 is written (AC-IAM-010-03-02).

A user who is not an administrator is allowed by a rule provider for a customer who is an administrator: when the request reaches the native action, the native action refuses it (Admin.Customers.Customers.NonAdminNotImpersonateAsAdminError); the IAM filter does not relax native checks (AC-IAM-010-03-03).
postconditions: The IAM impersonation filter allows it (BR-IAM-130), the storefront is shown as that customer and the native activity Impersonation.Started is written for both people (AC-IAM-010-03-01).

story: As a shopper, I want to deactivate my own account and reactivate it later, so that I control my account.
useCaseName: To deactivate my own account and reactivate it later
preconditions: A signed-in shopper.
trigger: The shopper chooses "Deactivate my account" and confirms with the password or a one-time code.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the shopper chooses "Deactivate my account" and confirms with the password or a one-time code.
2. The system responds: the account becomes inactive, all sessions end, message Iam.AccountDeactivated is shown, no data is deleted and marketing messages stop (BR-IAM-081) (AC-IAM-010-04-01).
3. The owner requests reactivation and confirms a code sent to the verified email or mobile number: the account becomes active again and message Iam.AccountReactivated is shown (AC-IAM-010-04-02).
exceptionFlow: The account was deactivated by staff: when the owner requests reactivation, self-reactivation is refused and message Iam.ContactSupport is shown (AC-IAM-010-04-03).
postconditions: The account becomes inactive, all sessions end, message Iam.AccountDeactivated is shown, no data is deleted and marketing messages stop (BR-IAM-081) (AC-IAM-010-04-01).

story: As an auditor, I want every staff action on user accounts to be recorded, so that misuse can be traced.
useCaseName: Every staff action on user accounts to be recorded
preconditions: Staff change a customer record, its roles or its addresses.
trigger: The change is saved.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the change is saved.
2. The system responds: the platform audit trail (SEC-004) stores old and new values and the native activity EditCustomer is written (AC-IAM-010-05-01).
3. The page is shown: a read-access event AUD-IAM-010 is written (BR-IAM-080) (AC-IAM-010-05-02).
postconditions: A read-access event AUD-IAM-010 is written (BR-IAM-080) (AC-IAM-010-05-02).

story: As a client administrator, I want to invite staff by email so that they set their own password, set up MFA and accept the terms before first use, so that no one receives a password from someone else.
useCaseName: To invite staff by email so that they set their own password, set up MFA and accept the terms before first use
preconditions: A user holds Identity.Core.AccessGovernance.CreateEditDelete.
trigger: The user invites email E with chosen roles.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the user invites email E with chosen roles.

2. The system responds: an invitation email with a single-use link is sent (message template Iam.Invitation.Email, default text Iam.Invitation); the link is valid for the configured days and no customer record exists yet (AC-IAM-011-01-01).

3. The invitee opens it, sets a password that meets IAM-003, sets up MFA where a role requires it (IAM-004) and accepts the current terms (IAM-016): the account is created as Registered with the invited roles and the invitation becomes Accepted (AUD-IAM-017) (AC-IAM-011-01-02).
exceptionFlow: An expired, revoked or already used link: when someone opens it, no account is created and message Iam.InvitationExpired is shown (AC-IAM-011-01-03).
postconditions: The account is created as Registered with the invited roles and the invitation becomes Accepted (AUD-IAM-017) (AC-IAM-011-01-02).

story: As a manager, I want to confirm regularly that each person still needs their access, so that access that is no longer needed is removed.
useCaseName: To confirm regularly that each person still needs their access
preconditions: An access-review campaign is started for a set of roles with a reviewer for each role.
trigger: The campaign opens.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the campaign opens.

2. The system responds: each reviewer sees the members of their roles and records Keep or Revoke for each; Revoke removes the role mapping through ICustomerService; every decision is audited (AUD-IAM-009) (AC-IAM-011-02-01).
3. The deadline task runs: the undecided items become Overdue and are listed to administrators; no role is removed automatically (AC-IAM-011-02-02).
postconditions: The undecided items become Overdue and are listed to administrators; no role is removed automatically (AC-IAM-011-02-02).

story: As an auditor, I want an access audit report with role assignments, privileged accounts and MFA status, so that I can check access controls.
useCaseName: An access audit report with role assignments, privileged accounts and MFA status
preconditions: A user holds Identity.Core.AccessReports.View.
trigger: The user runs the access audit report.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the user runs the access audit report.

2. The system responds: one row per user shows: roles, whether the user is privileged (holds Security.AccessAdminPanel or a permission in the privileged list), MFA status (provider selected, none, or required but not set up — from the SelectedMultiFactorAuthenticationProvider attribute), last login and Active; the report can be exported to CSV and XLSX (AC-IAM-011-03-01).
3. It runs: only users that meet the privileged definition are listed (AC-IAM-011-03-02).
postconditions: Only users that meet the privileged definition are listed (AC-IAM-011-03-02).

story: As a security officer, I want every login, failed login, logout, MFA challenge, password change, MFA enrolment, role change and access denial recorded with time, IP address and outcome, so that I can investigate account misuse.
useCaseName: Every login, failed login, logout, MFA challenge, password change, MFA enrolment, role change and access denial recorded with time, IP address and outcome
preconditions: The IAM plugin is installed.
trigger: The configuration is applied.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the configuration is applied.

2. The system responds: the native activity types PublicStore.SuccessfulLogin, PublicStore.FailedLogin and PublicStore.Logout are enabled (they are disabled at native install) and CustomerSettings.StoreIpAddresses is on (AC-IAM-012-01-01).

3. The event completes: an AuthEvent is written with UTC time, customer (or the identifier tried), IP address, user agent, channel and outcome, and is copied to the platform audit trail (AUD-IAM-018) (AC-IAM-012-01-02).

4. Any user, including an administrator, tries to edit or delete one: no screen or service offers edit or delete; the native activity log can be deleted (Customers.ActivityLogDelete) but the copy in SEC-004 cannot (AC-IAM-012-01-03).
postconditions: No screen or service offers edit or delete; the native activity log can be deleted (Customers.ActivityLogDelete) but the copy in SEC-004 cannot (AC-IAM-012-01-03).

story: As a security officer, I want unusual login patterns flagged, such as many failures or a login from a new country, so that account takeover is detected early.
useCaseName: Unusual login patterns flagged, such as many failures or a login from a new country
preconditions: A failed-login rule (more than N failures in M minutes for one account or one IP address) is active.
trigger: The rule is exceeded.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the rule is exceeded.
2. The system responds: a suspicious-login flag is raised, the security officer is notified and the flag appears in the console (SM-IAM-12) (AC-IAM-012-02-01).

3. A customer logs in from a country (IGeoLookupService with the bundled GeoLite2-Country database) not seen for that customer in the look-back period: a flag is raised and, if the setting is on, the customer receives message template Iam.NewCountryLogin.CustomerNotification (AC-IAM-012-02-02).
4. The security officer confirms it: the officer can force the user off (IAM-006) and the flag becomes Confirmed; dismissing needs a reason (AUD-IAM-016) (AC-IAM-012-02-03).
postconditions: The officer can force the user off (IAM-006) and the flag becomes Confirmed; dismissing needs a reason (AUD-IAM-016) (AC-IAM-012-02-03).

story: As a security officer, I want authentication events available to our security monitoring system and to auditors, so that monitoring and audit can use them.
useCaseName: Authentication events available to our security monitoring system and to auditors
preconditions: A user holds Identity.Core.AuthEvents.View.
trigger: The user filters by date, customer, IP address and outcome.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the user filters by date, customer, IP address and outcome.
2. The system responds: matching events are listed and can be exported to CSV (AC-IAM-012-03-01).
3. Authentication events are written: they are sent through IC-SEC-02 in the agreed format (AC-IAM-012-03-02).
postconditions: They are sent through IC-SEC-02 in the agreed format (AC-IAM-012-03-02).

story: As a shopper or member of staff, I want to log in with a fingerprint, face recognition or a device security key instead of a password, so that logging in is faster and safer.
useCaseName: To log in with a fingerprint, face recognition or a device security key instead of a password
preconditions: A signed-in user on a device that supports passkeys.
trigger: The user registers a passkey.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the user registers a passkey.
2. The system responds: the public key credential is stored for the user and listed under My account, where it can be removed (AC-IAM-013-01-01).
3. The user chooses "log in with passkey" and the device verifies the user: the user is signed in through SignInCustomerAsync without a password (AC-IAM-013-01-02).
4. The login page is shown: password and one-time code login remain available (AC-IAM-013-01-03).

5. The user logs in with a passkey that verified the user on the device: the login completes and no second-factor prompt is shown, because the passkey user verification counts as the second factor required by IAM-004 (AC-IAM-013-01-04).
postconditions: The public key credential is stored for the user and listed under My account, where it can be removed (AC-IAM-013-01-01).

story: As a shopper, I want to keep my name and contact details up to date, so that orders and messages reach me.
useCaseName: To keep my name and contact details up to date
preconditions: A signed-in shopper on the My account information page.
trigger: The shopper changes name, phone or email and saves.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the shopper changes name, phone or email and saves.

2. The system responds: the values are saved; an email change follows the native revalidation when registration type is EmailValidation; with GdprSettings.LogUserProfileChanges on, the change is written to the GDPR log (AC-IAM-014-01-01).
3. The shopper changes the number: the new number replaces the identifier only after a code sent to it is entered correctly (AC-IAM-014-01-02).
postconditions: The values are saved; an email change follows the native revalidation when registration type is EmailValidation; with GdprSettings.LogUserProfileChanges on, the change is written to the GDPR log (AC-IAM-014-01-01).

story: As a shopper, I want to save several delivery addresses and choose a default, so that checkout is faster and deliveries go to the right place.
useCaseName: To save several delivery addresses and choose a default
preconditions: A signed-in shopper in My account Addresses.
trigger: The shopper adds, edits or deletes addresses.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the shopper adds, edits or deletes addresses.
2. The system responds: each change is saved and the list shows all saved addresses (AC-IAM-014-02-01).
3. The shopper marks one as default: that address is shown first and marked as default; checkout pre-selects it (CHK, carried) (AC-IAM-014-02-02).
4. The shopper reaches the address step: the saved addresses are offered without retyping (AC-IAM-014-02-03).
postconditions: Each change is saved and the list shows all saved addresses (AC-IAM-014-02-01).

story: As a shopper, I want to save a preferred pickup point such as a post office, so that pickup orders go there without choosing each time.
useCaseName: To save a preferred pickup point such as a post office
preconditions: Pickup points exist (PRD-LOG-003, StorePickupPoint).
trigger: The shopper selects one as preferred in My account.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the shopper selects one as preferred in My account.
2. The system responds: it is saved; the checkout pickup option pre-selects it (CHK, carried) (AC-IAM-015-01-01).
3. The shopper next opens checkout or My account: the preference is cleared and the shopper is asked to choose another with message Iam.PickupPointUnavailable (AC-IAM-015-01-02).
postconditions: It is saved; the checkout pickup option pre-selects it (CHK, carried) (AC-IAM-015-01-01).

story: As a shopper, I want to choose how I want to be contacted (SMS, email, app), so that messages arrive the way I prefer.
useCaseName: To choose how I want to be contacted (SMS, email, app)
preconditions: The channels configured in the notification engine (TRK-005) are listed.
trigger: The shopper selects a preferred channel.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the shopper selects a preferred channel.
2. The system responds: it is saved and TRK-006 uses it for every event that has no event-level preference (AC-IAM-015-02-01).
3. The shopper opens the channel choice: the app channel is not offered (AC-IAM-015-02-02).
postconditions: It is saved and TRK-006 uses it for every event that has no event-level preference (AC-IAM-015-02-01).

story: As a shopper, I want to accept the terms of use and the privacy policy when I register, so that the agreement is clear from the start.
useCaseName: To accept the terms of use and the privacy policy when I register
preconditions: Current versions of the terms of use and the privacy policy are published.
trigger: A person registers by web, mobile number or through an agent.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: a person registers by web, mobile number or through an agent.
2. The system responds: registration cannot complete without acceptance, and a PolicyAcceptance row records policy, version, time, channel, IP address and agent (if any) (AC-IAM-016-01-01).

3. An acceptance is recorded: the version number stored is the Effective version returned by IC-MKT-03 GetEffectivePolicyVersion at that time; IAM stores no policy text and creates no version (BR-IAM-091) (AC-IAM-016-01-02).
4. An acceptance is recorded: it is stored with version "unversioned" and the topic and time, and no re-acceptance prompt can be raised for that policy (AC-IAM-016-01-03).
postconditions: The version number stored is the Effective version returned by IC-MKT-03 GetEffectivePolicyVersion at that time; IAM stores no policy text and creates no version (BR-IAM-091) (AC-IAM-016-01-02).

story: As a shopper, I want to be asked to accept again when a new version is published, so that I know about changes that affect me.
useCaseName: To be asked to accept again when a new version is published
preconditions: IC-MKT-03 GetEffectivePolicyVersion returns a new Effective version of a policy with the MKT-008 flag "re-acceptance required" set.
trigger: A registered user who accepted an older version makes a request.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: a registered user who accepted an older version makes a request.

2. The system responds: the user is redirected to the acceptance page with message Iam.TermsUpdated until the new version is accepted; logout and the policy pages stay reachable (BR-IAM-091) (AC-IAM-016-02-01).
3. Users make requests: no prompt is shown; later acceptances (for example at registration) record the new version; IAM keeps no re-acceptance flag of its own (AC-IAM-016-02-03).

4. The owner user of an approved seller makes a request in the seller portal: the IAM re-acceptance filter redirects the owner to the acceptance page until the new version is accepted; the acceptance is stored with customer, vendor and version (AC-IAM-016-02-04).
postconditions: The IAM re-acceptance filter redirects the owner to the acceptance page until the new version is accepted; the acceptance is stored with customer, vendor and version (AC-IAM-016-02-04).

story: As a member of support staff, I want to see when a customer accepted each version and gave or withdrew each consent, so that I can resolve complaints with evidence.
useCaseName: To see when a customer accepted each version and gave or withdrew each consent
preconditions: A user holds Identity.Core.ConsentTrail.View.
trigger: The user opens the consent trail of a customer.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the user opens the consent trail of a customer.
2. The system responds: PolicyAcceptance rows and the native GDPR log consent entries (ConsentAgree, ConsentDisagree) are listed in time order, read-only (AC-IAM-016-03-01).
exceptionFlow: A CRM-003 agent holds Identity.Core.ConsentTrail.View: when the 360-degree view calls IC-IAM-05 GetConsentTrail for the customer, the same entries are returned (policy, version, decision, channel, time; consent agree or disagree with time), read-only; without the permission the call is refused (AC-IAM-016-03-02).
postconditions: PolicyAcceptance rows and the native GDPR log consent entries (ConsentAgree, ConsentDisagree) are listed in time order, read-only (AC-IAM-016-03-01).

story: As a shopper, I want to give or withdraw my consent to marketing and to cookies and tracking, so that my choices are respected.
useCaseName: To give or withdraw my consent to marketing and to cookies and tracking
preconditions: Consents (GdprConsent) are configured with DisplayOnCustomerInfoPage.
trigger: The shopper ticks or clears a consent on the My account information page and saves.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the shopper ticks or clears a consent on the My account information page and saves.
2. The system responds: the GDPR log records ConsentAgree or ConsentDisagree with time; a withdrawn marketing consent stops marketing messages from the next send (AC-IAM-017-01-01).
3. The shopper changes cookie choices from the footer link: the new choice applies from the next page (see SEC-007 (REQ-MPC-FR-010)) (AC-IAM-017-01-02).

4. The withdrawal is saved: the modules registered for that consent are told through IC-IAM-08 ConsentWithdrawn and stop the processing from the next request; the module decides whether stored data is deleted (AC-IAM-017-01-03).
postconditions: The modules registered for that consent are told through IC-IAM-08 ConsentWithdrawn and stop the processing from the next request; the module decides whether stored data is deleted (AC-IAM-017-01-03).

story: As a shopper, I want to download the personal data held about me, so that I know what is held.
useCaseName: To download the personal data held about me
preconditions: GdprSettings.GdprEnabled is on.
trigger: The shopper chooses "Export my data" on the GDPR tools page.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the shopper chooses "Export my data" on the GDPR tools page.
2. The system responds: the native XLSX export is downloaded, the GDPR log records ExportData, and a second file lists the personal data held in product plugin tables (Proposed) (AC-IAM-017-02-01).
postconditions: The native XLSX export is downloaded, the GDPR log records ExportData, and a second file lists the personal data held in product plugin tables (Proposed) (AC-IAM-017-02-01).

story: As a shopper, I want to ask for my personal data used for orders and deliveries to be corrected, so that my orders and deliveries use correct details.
useCaseName: To ask for my personal data used for orders and deliveries to be corrected
preconditions: A signed-in shopper.
trigger: The shopper submits a correction request naming the field, the current value, the requested value and a reason.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the shopper submits a correction request naming the field, the current value, the requested value and a reason.

2. The system responds: a PrivacyRequest of type Correction is created as Received, its due date is set from the country profile (SEC-012) and message Iam.CorrectionRequestReceived is shown (AC-IAM-017-03-01).

3. A user holding Customers.GDPRManage approves it: the customer field or saved address is updated, the shopper is notified, the GDPR log records ProfileChanged and AUD-IAM-011 is written; addresses already copied to placed orders are not changed by this flow (AC-IAM-017-03-02).
postconditions: A PrivacyRequest of type Correction is created as Received, its due date is set from the country profile (SEC-012) and message Iam.CorrectionRequestReceived is shown (AC-IAM-017-03-01).

story: As a shopper, I want to ask for my account to be deleted, so that my personal data is removed where the law allows.
useCaseName: To ask for my account to be deleted
preconditions: GdprSettings.GdprEnabled is on.
trigger: The shopper chooses "Delete account" on the GDPR tools page.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the shopper chooses "Delete account" on the GDPR tools page.

2. The system responds: the native flow logs DeleteCustomer in the GDPR log and sends Customer.Gdpr.DeleteRequest to the store owner, and a PrivacyRequest of type Deletion is opened with its due date (AC-IAM-017-04-01).

3. A user holding Customers.GDPRManage runs the native GDPR delete: the IAM override of IGdprService.PermanentDeleteCustomerAsync also clears the personal fields that native code leaves (BR-IAM-092) and personal data in IAM plugin tables; orders and invoices are kept under the retention rules (PLT-020, SEC-012); AUD-IAM-011 is written (AC-IAM-017-04-02).

4. The IAM override of IGdprService.PermanentDeleteCustomerAsync runs: each provider is called inside the same operation and reports Erased or Failed; a Failed provider leaves the PrivacyRequest InProgress with the provider named, and the request is not Completed (BR-IAM-092) (AC-IAM-017-04-03).
postconditions: Each provider is called inside the same operation and reports Erased or Failed; a Failed provider leaves the PrivacyRequest InProgress with the provider named, and the request is not Completed (BR-IAM-092) (AC-IAM-017-04-03).

story: As a privacy officer, I want each privacy request to be handled within the deadline for the country, with evidence, so that we meet our data-protection duties.
basis: Inference from REQ-KTDA-LEG-001 (local data-protection law; law names are inference, DP-01); REQ-MPC-FR-022
useCaseName: Each privacy request to be handled within the deadline for the country, with evidence
preconditions: A privacy request is open.
trigger: Its due date (from the country profile, SEC-012) is reached without completion.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: its due date (from the country profile, SEC-012) is reached without completion.
2. The system responds: it is marked Overdue and the privacy officer is notified (AC-IAM-017-05-01).
3. The user opens the privacy trail of a customer: consent changes, exports, correction and deletion requests are listed with dates and outcomes (AC-IAM-017-05-02).
postconditions: Consent changes, exports, correction and deletion requests are listed with dates and outcomes (AC-IAM-017-05-02).

story: As a KTDA analytics user, I want analytics data to be collected only with a lawful basis, so that our customer insights are lawful.
useCaseName: Analytics data to be collected only with a lawful basis
preconditions: A visitor has not accepted the analytics cookie category.
trigger: Pages are shown.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: pages are shown.
2. The system responds: no analytics widget is rendered for that visitor and no analytics profile is built (SEC-007 gating) (AC-IAM-017-06-01).
postconditions: No analytics widget is rendered for that visitor and no analytics profile is built (SEC-007 gating) (AC-IAM-017-06-01).

story: As a shopper, I want to see recent logins, important profile changes and payment attempts on my account, so that I can spot suspicious activity myself.
useCaseName: To see recent logins, important profile changes and payment attempts on my account
preconditions: A signed-in shopper.
trigger: The shopper opens Account activity in My account.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the shopper opens Account activity in My account.

2. The system responds: the page lists, newest first and for the configured look-back period: logins and failed logins (AuthEvent), changes to name, email, phone, password, MFA and addresses (field names, not values), and payment attempts with time, method and status (PAY PaymentTransaction) (AC-IAM-018-01-01).

3. They are shown to the shopper: the IP address is partly masked: when SEC-014 is delivered its masking rule applies; until then (P1) the last octet of an IPv4 address, or the last 80 bits of an IPv6 address, are replaced by zeros (Proposed) (AC-IAM-018-01-02).
postconditions: The page lists, newest first and for the configured look-back period: logins and failed logins (AuthEvent), changes to name, email, phone, password, MFA and addresses (field names, not values), and payment attempts with time, method and status (PAY PaymentTransaction) (AC-IAM-018-01-01).

story: As a shopper, I want to see when staff accessed my data, so that I know who looked at my data.
useCaseName: To see when staff accessed my data
preconditions: Staff opened or changed the customer record, an order or an address of the customer (AUD-IAM-010, SEC-004).
trigger: The shopper opens Account activity.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the shopper opens Account activity.
2. The system responds: a "staff access" entry is shown with date and, as the setting says, the staff member name or role (AC-IAM-018-02-01).
postconditions: A "staff access" entry is shown with date and, as the setting says, the staff member name or role (AC-IAM-018-02-01).

story: As an authorised administrator, I want to see the same history for a customer, so that I can help with account concerns.
useCaseName: To see the same history for a customer
preconditions: A user holds Customers.CustomersView.
trigger: The user opens the customer in admin.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the user opens the customer in admin.
2. The system responds: an Account activity tab shows the same entries (AC-IAM-018-03-01).
postconditions: An Account activity tab shows the same entries (AC-IAM-018-03-01).

story: As a Malawi Post integration manager, I want customer accounts kept in step with our other internal systems through the Integration Layer, so that there are no duplicate or conflicting customer records.
useCaseName: Customer accounts kept in step with our other internal systems through the Integration Layer
preconditions: Synchronisation is enabled for a set of fields.
trigger: A customer is registered, updated, deactivated or deleted.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: a customer is registered, updated, deactivated or deleted.

2. The system responds: an IntegrationMessage with channel "account sync" is written to the INT-004 outbox through IC-INT-09 Enqueue (the IAM event consumer for CustomerRegisteredEvent and EntityInsertedEvent / EntityUpdatedEvent of Customer only enqueues, BR-INT-010) and the INT delivery task sends it to the Integration Layer adapter (IC-IAM-03 PublishAccountChange) (AC-IAM-019-01-01).

3. The INT-004 retry policy applies: the message is retried (SM-INT-01); after the last retry it becomes DeadLettered and appears in the INT dead-letter list (Integrations.Core.Messages.View); IAM keeps no outbox of its own (BR-IAM-100) (AC-IAM-019-01-02).

4. It is processed: only the configured fields are updated; if the platform value changed after the core-system version, the configured system of record wins and the conflict is logged (AC-IAM-019-01-03).
5. The deletion completes: the core system receives an erasure notice for that customer (AC-IAM-019-01-04).
postconditions: The message is retried (SM-INT-01); after the last retry it becomes DeadLettered and appears in the INT dead-letter list (Integrations.Core.Messages.View); IAM keeps no outbox of its own (BR-IAM-100) (AC-IAM-019-01-02).

story: As a compliance officer, I want identity details checked against official or mobile-network sources where a process requires KYC, so that buyers and sellers are who they say they are.
useCaseName: Identity details checked against official or mobile-network sources where a process requires KYC
preconditions: A mobile-money KYC adapter is available.
trigger: A person chooses to verify with the mobile number.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: a person chooses to verify with the mobile number.
2. The system responds: the adapter returns the match result from the mobile-money registration and it is recorded as above (AC-IAM-020-01-02).
3. The result is recorded: the case goes to the manual review queue; a user holding Identity.Core.Verification.CreateEditDelete decides it with a reason (AUD-IAM-015) (AC-IAM-020-01-03).

4. The case is decided: the AI output is shown to the reviewer as a suggestion only; the result Verified or NotVerified is set by the adapter or by a reviewer holding Identity.Core.Verification.CreateEditDelete, never by the AI output alone (BR-AI-002, BR-IAM-110) (AC-IAM-020-01-05).
exceptionFlow: A process is configured to require KYC: when a person submits an identity type and number, the framework calls the adapter for the country (IC-IAM-02) and records the result Verified, NotVerified, Inconclusive or Unavailable with the adapter reference and time; identity document images are not stored by the framework (BR-IAM-110) (AC-IAM-020-01-01).

SEL-004 calls IC-IAM-02 Verify for a seller (check type, country, identifier, name): when the adapter answers, the result is returned as Verified, NotVerified, Inconclusive or Unavailable with the adapter reference (the product standard values, owner decision); SEL stores its own copy and handles Inconclusive as manual review under its own maker-checker rule (BR-SEL-007); IAM opens no manual review case for checks requested by SEL (AC-IAM-020-01-04).
postconditions: The adapter returns the match result from the mobile-money registration and it is recorded as above (AC-IAM-020-01-02).

story: Technical enabler. As a member of the platform team, I want each country to connect through its own adapter on one framework, so that a new country is added without rebuilding.
useCaseName: Each country to connect through its own adapter on one framework
preconditions: A new adapter implements IC-IAM-02.
trigger: It is installed and configured for a country.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: it is installed and configured for a country.
2. The system responds: it is used for that country without change to the framework (AC-IAM-020-02-01).
postconditions: It is used for that country without change to the framework (AC-IAM-020-02-01).

story: As a shopper, I want to see my past orders with status, items, totals and tracking references, so that I can follow and check my orders.
useCaseName: To see my past orders with status, items, totals and tracking references
preconditions: A customer has orders.
trigger: The customer opens Orders in My account.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the customer opens Orders in My account.
2. The system responds: each order is listed with number, date, status and total; the details page shows items, totals and shipments with tracking numbers (AC-IAM-021-01-01).
postconditions: Each order is listed with number, date, status and total; the details page shows items, totals and shipments with tracking numbers (AC-IAM-021-01-01).

story: As a shopper, I want to view and download receipts and invoices for my orders, so that I keep my own records.
useCaseName: To view and download receipts and invoices for my orders
preconditions: An order details page.
trigger: The customer chooses the PDF invoice.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the customer chooses the PDF invoice.
2. The system responds: the native PDF invoice is downloaded (AC-IAM-021-02-01).
postconditions: The native PDF invoice is downloaded (AC-IAM-021-02-01).

story: As a business buyer, I want to see my quotes and returns and export my history to a spreadsheet, so that I can work with it offline.
useCaseName: To see my quotes and returns and export my history to a spreadsheet
preconditions: The bundled Misc.RFQ plugin is active and the customer has quotes or return requests.
trigger: The customer opens My account.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the customer opens My account.
2. The system responds: quotes and return requests are listed in their own pages (AC-IAM-021-03-01).
3. The customer chooses Export: a CSV or XLSX file of the filtered list is downloaded (AC-IAM-021-03-02).
postconditions: A CSV or XLSX file of the filtered list is downloaded (AC-IAM-021-03-02).

story: As a returning shopper, I want to order again from a past order, so that repeat purchase is quick.
useCaseName: To order again from a past order
preconditions: OrderSettings.IsReOrderAllowed is on.
trigger: The customer chooses Re-order on a past order.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the customer chooses Re-order on a past order.
2. The system responds: the items of that order are added to the basket (AC-IAM-021-04-01).
postconditions: The items of that order are added to the basket (AC-IAM-021-04-01).

story: As a business buyer, I want a company account where several of our staff share addresses and order history, so that we buy as a team.
basis: D; Inference from REQ-KTDA-CUS-002 (B2B buyers; PH-INF)
useCaseName: A company account where several of our staff share addresses and order history
actors: CHK-016 (B2B on-account payment and credit limits)
preconditions: Company C has members.
trigger: A member places an order.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: a member places an order.
2. The system responds: the order is linked to C and visible to members with the view right; the shared company addresses are offered at checkout (AC-IAM-022-01-01).
3. It calls IC-IAM-07 GetCompanyOfCustomer: it receives the CompanyId, the company status and the company role of the customer, or "no company" (AC-IAM-022-01-03).
exceptionFlow: A customer is not a member of C: when the customer opens an order of C by its address, access is denied (AC-IAM-022-01-02).
postconditions: The order is linked to C and visible to members with the view right; the shared company addresses are offered at checkout (AC-IAM-022-01-01).

story: As a company administrator, I want to give each member a company role such as buyer, approver or company administrator, so that each person does only their part.
useCaseName: To give each member a company role such as buyer, approver or company administrator
preconditions: A company administrator.
trigger: The administrator adds a member by email invitation and gives a company role.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the administrator adds a member by email invitation and gives a company role.
2. The system responds: the member gets the rights of that role in C: buyer orders, approver approves (CHK-018), company administrator manages members (BR-IAM-120) (AC-IAM-022-02-01).
3. The change is saved: the member loses access to C data; orders the member placed stay with C (AC-IAM-022-02-02).

4. A buyer of C submits a cart above the threshold of the buyer role: CHK-018 reads the company role of the buyer through IC-IAM-07; thresholds are stored by CHK-018, not by IAM (BR-IAM-120) (AC-IAM-022-02-04).
exceptionFlow: CAT-040 (P2) is delivered, has registered a membership provider and created the per-company system customer role of C (before CAT-040 no provider is registered and membership changes call none): when a member is added to or removed from C, IAM calls the provider (IC-IAM-07 OnMembershipChanged) inside the same save, so CAT adds or removes the mapping of the member to that role through ICustomerService; if the provider fails the membership change is not saved (AC-IAM-022-02-03).
postconditions: CHK-018 reads the company role of the buyer through IC-IAM-07; thresholds are stored by CHK-018, not by IAM (BR-IAM-120) (AC-IAM-022-02-04).

story: As a business, I want to apply for a trade account with company details, tax number and documents, so that we can buy at trade terms.
basis: D; Inference from REQ-KTDA-CUS-002 (B2B buyers; PH-INF)
useCaseName: To apply for a trade account with company details, tax number and documents
preconditions: The trade application form is configured.
trigger: A business submits company name, registration number, tax or VAT number and the required documents.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: a business submits company name, registration number, tax or VAT number and the required documents.

2. The system responds: a TradeApplication is created as Received with the files stored as Download records (native customer attributes do not support file upload) and message Iam.TradeApplicationReceived is shown (AC-IAM-023-01-01).
exceptionFlow: A document attached to the application has a file type or size outside the ADM-008 upload policy of the context "trade application document" (registered by IAM at installation through IC-ADM-08 RegisterUploadContext; IAM checks each file through IC-ADM-08 CheckUpload before storing it): when the form is posted, the file is refused by the ADM-008 policy before anything is stored (BR-ADM-060); IAM adds no type or size check of its own (AC-IAM-023-01-02).
postconditions: A TradeApplication is created as Received with the files stored as Download records (native customer attributes do not support file upload) and message Iam.TradeApplicationReceived is shown (AC-IAM-023-01-01).

story: As a client sales staff member, I want to approve applications before trade prices are shown, so that trade terms go only to checked businesses.
useCaseName: To approve applications before trade prices are shown
preconditions: A user holds Identity.Core.TradeAccounts.CreateEditDelete.
trigger: The user approves an application.
basicFlow: 1. Trigger: the user approves an application.

2. The system responds: the customer gets the TradeBuyer role, a company account is created (IAM-022), trade prices limited to that role (tier prices by CustomerRoleId, ACL) become visible and the applicant receives message template Iam.TradeApplicationApproved.CustomerNotification (AUD-IAM-013) (AC-IAM-023-02-01).

As a manager, I want a home dashboard with order and customer figures, in text and charts, so that I see the state of the business when I sign in.

As a shopper, I want to move through the category tree in several ways, so that I find products easily whatever my experience.

story: As a member of marketing staff, I want to build menus, sliders, product carousels and curated collections without developers, so that promotions run on time.
As a member of marketing staff, I want banners and featured categories that appear and disappear on set dates, so that campaigns start and stop by themselves.
As a member of marketing staff, I want campaign landing pages made of configurable blocks, so that each campaign has its own page.
As a shopper, I want labels such as "New" or "Sale" on product pictures, so that I notice offers.
As a shopper, I want related products, "customers also bought", recently viewed items and new arrivals, so that I discover more products.
As a shopper who has given consent, I want recommendations and search results ordered by what I browse and buy, so that suggestions are more relevant to me.
As a shopper, I want no personal data used for recommendations unless I agree, so that my choice is respected.
As a shopper, I want to save products to a wish list, share it by email and move items to the cart later, so that I can come back and buy later.
As a shopper, I want to save a search and be told when new matching products appear, so that I come back at the right moment.
As a shopper, I want to watch a product and be told when its price drops or it is back in stock, so that I buy when it suits me.
As a shopper, I want to see my recent searches and recently viewed products and repeat a search with one tap, so that I save time.
As a shopper, I want to put chosen products side by side and compare their details, so that I make a better-informed choice.
As a shopper, I want the best matches ranked first, including synonyms, other word forms and small typing mistakes, so that I find what I mean, not only exact words.
As a shopper, I want to search in my language with a fallback when nothing matches, so that I can search in any language the shop offers.
As a catalogue manager, I want to set boosting rules by category, featured status and location, with every change recorded, so that we tune results without developers and can show who changed what.
As a shopper, I want lists of best sellers, most viewed and trending products by region or category, so that I see what is popular.
As a member of marketing staff, I want those lists to refresh by themselves, so that I do not maintain them by hand.
As a catalogue manager, I want to propose a new category, a change or the retirement of a category, so that the category structure stays tidy as the catalogue grows.
As a catalogue manager, I want proposals approved by another person, with every step recorded, so that changes are controlled and can be audited.
As a shopper, I want badges such as "verified" or "top rated" on sellers, so that I trust the seller.
As a member of marketing staff, I want to feature sellers for set dates, so that good sellers are rewarded.
As a shopper, I want product cards in lists to show the expected delivery time and whether pickup is available, so that I choose by delivery speed before opening the product.
As a shopper, I want search results without unpublished, suspended or out-of-stock items, according to rules the client sets, so that I do not see things I cannot buy.
As a shopper, I want a separate area for the operator's own services such as postal, logistics or financial services, so that services are easy to find apart from goods.
As a member of marketing staff, I want web analytics on what people click and buy after searching or browsing, so that we see what works and improve the shop.
As a shopper with a disability, I want to use search and menus with a keyboard only and with a screen reader, so that I can find products.
As a shopper on a weak mobile connection, I want search to show a message and let me retry instead of failing, so that I can still search.
As a channel system (USSD, SMS or kiosk), I want a search service I can call, so that customers without smartphones can still search.
As a business buyer, I want one search box that finds products, my orders, my quotes and my own records, so that I find anything from one place.
As a shopper, I want search to answer quickly and show new or changed products at once, so that I see current stock and prices.

As a shopper, I want quick product preview, a "buy now" button, "email a friend", a delivery-cost estimate on the product page and links to the previous and next product, so that I buy faster and more easily.
As a service provider, I want to sell a service at a fixed price, so that simple services are bought like any item.
As a service provider, I want to price a service per hour, day or week, so that time-based services are charged for the time booked.
As a service provider, I want to price a service per unit such as per hectare or per parcel, with the unit shown next to the price, so that the customer pays for the quantity of work.
As a service provider, I want to show a from-price when the final price depends on the options chosen, so that customers see the lowest price before choosing.
As a business buyer, I want to request a quote for a service marked price on request and then order at the quoted price, so that custom work is priced for my needs.
As a service provider, I want to record who or what delivers each service — staff, teams, equipment or vehicles, so that bookings are matched to real capacity.
As a service provider, I want to record qualifications and certifications with expiry dates and the services each requires, so that only qualified resources are booked.
As a service provider, I want to set working hours, closures and the area each resource covers, so that bookings are only offered when and where a resource can work.
As a client operations staff, I want bookings to be accepted only when a qualified, free resource covering the place has capacity, so that no booking is taken that cannot be delivered.
As a client administrator, I want service providers to be a supplier category, so that service-provider rules apply only to them.
As a shopper, I want to reschedule my booking to another free slot within the rules, so that I can fit the service around my plans.
As a shopper, I want to cancel my booking and see any fee before I confirm, so that I know what I will get back.
As a client operations staff, I want to set per service a free-change period, a cancellation fee after it and a maximum number of reschedules, so that rules are fair and predictable.
As a service provider, I want to record that the customer did not come, and have the no-show policy applied, so that my time is protected.
As a shopper, I want a full refund and an offer to rebook when the provider does not turn up, so that I am not penalised for the provider failure.
As a client operations staff, I want to set per service whether a booking needs full payment, a deposit or no payment upfront, so that the payment rule fits the service.
As a shopper, I want to pay the deposit when I book and the balance later, so that I secure the slot without paying everything at once.
As a shopper, I want to pay the balance online or at an outlet before the due point, so that the booking is fully paid.
As a member of finance staff, I want deposits to be refunded or kept according to the cancellation policy, so that deposit handling is consistent.
As a service provider, I want to move a service order through Requested, Confirmed, Scheduled, In progress and Completed, so that everyone sees where the service stands.
As a shopper, I want to confirm that the service was delivered, or report that it was not, so that there is a record before money moves.
As a member of finance staff, I want the provider to become eligible for payout only after the customer confirms, so that money changes hands only for delivered services.
As a shopper, I want a refund to start under the client policy when a service failed, so that I get my money back for a service not delivered.
As a Malawi Post customer, I want to order Malawi Post services through an ordering flow that shows each step, so that I know each step of my service order.
As a shopper, I want to say where the service happens — at my site, at an outlet or remotely — when I book, so that the provider comes to the right place or contacts me the right way.
As a shopper, I want to place a pin on a map for my site, so that the provider finds places without a street address.
As a service provider, I want bookings only for places I cover, so that I do not receive bookings I cannot deliver.
As a shopper, I want to download an electronic item such as an e-document, licence or report after I pay, so that I get it at once without shipping.
As a client administrator, I want to limit the number of downloads and the days a download stays available, so that files are not shared without limit.
As a member of finance staff, I want a licence file per order line where a licence is sold, so that each buyer gets their own licence.
As a shopper, I want to find my downloads in My account and in the order email, so that I can download again within the limits.
As a shopper, I want to hire an item for chosen start and end dates and see the price for that length, so that I pay for the time I use.
As a shopper, I want only dates on which an item is free to be offered, so that my hire is not refused later.
As a service provider, I want to set how many units of an item I can hire out, so that bookings match my fleet.
As a shopper, I want a voucher or e-ticket with a code and QR code after I pay for a service, so that I can prove I paid.
As a service provider or outlet staff, I want to scan or type the code to check it and redeem it once, so that fraud is prevented.
As a Malawi Post customer, I want to buy tickets for partner services listed by Malawi Post, so that I can use the post office for ticketing.
As a shopper, I want reminders before my booked service, so that I do not miss it.
As a service provider, I want a feedback request sent after the service, so that I learn how to improve.
As a client operations staff, I want to set response and completion targets per service and service level, so that service orders have measurable promises.
As a client operations staff, I want each service order to be tracked against its targets and escalated when a target is at risk or missed, so that late services are acted on.
As a shopper, I want to see the promised response and completion time when I order, so that I know what to expect.

As a member of management, I want reports on bookings, provider utilisation, completed and cancelled services, no-shows and service-level performance, so that I see demand and where delivery must improve.
As a shopper, I want to track a parcel by its tracking number and see a timeline of where it has been, so that I know where my order is without calling support.
As a shopper, I want to share a tracking link with the recipient without showing my account, so that the recipient can follow the parcel.
As a shopper, I want the tracking page to refresh by itself and on request, so that I see the latest status.
As a registered shopper, I want a dashboard of my orders with the delivery status of each, so that I can track all my orders in one place.

As a member of logistics operations staff, I want tracking updates from our scanners, couriers and international postal systems collected in one place under one list of event names, so that we have one tracking picture whatever carries the parcel.
As a client administrator, I want a standard event dictionary with a mapping for each external system, so that every source speaks the same language.
As a member of logistics operations staff, I want parcels that missed an expected scan flagged for review, so that delays are caught early.
As a client administrator, I want tracking events kept and archived according to retention rules, so that we meet compliance and keep the store manageable.
As a member of logistics operations staff, I want a track-and-trace screen to find any order or parcel and see its full history, so that I can answer stakeholders.
As a member of Malawi Post field or hub staff, I want to scan parcels at collection, sorting and delivery with a phone app, so that every hand-over of a parcel is recorded.
As a member of logistics operations staff, I want each scan to carry the staff and device identifiers, so that we know who scanned what and on which device.
As a member of field staff, I want to keep scanning without signal and add location, photos, voice notes and video as evidence, so that work continues in remote areas and evidence is kept.

As a client administrator, I want event-triggered emails (order placed, shipped and others) from templates that fill in details such as name and order number, in each language and shop, so that customers are kept informed automatically.
As a client administrator, I want bounced emails detected and the address flagged, so that we stop sending to dead addresses and use another channel.
As a client administrator, I want to configure email templates and the email channel from the admin, so that we change wording without developers.
As a client administrator, I want to write a message once per event and have it sent by SMS, email, app notification or WhatsApp, so that messages are consistent on every channel.
As a shopper, I want messages in my language, so that I understand them.
As a client administrator, I want a fallback channel when the first channel fails, so that important messages still arrive.
As a shopper, I want an order confirmation after I order and a message whenever my order status changes, so that I always know where my order stands.
As a client administrator, I want to configure content per event and channel and switch channels on or off, so that each client uses the channels it has.
As a shopper, I want to choose which messages I receive and on which channels, so that I get useful messages, not spam.
As a shopper, I want to set quiet hours, so that I am not disturbed at night.
As a shopper, I want to subscribe to or unsubscribe from updates for a single order, so that I follow only the orders I care about.
As a client administrator, I want to configure suppression rules: default quiet hours and limits on how many messages a customer receives, so that customers are not overwhelmed.

As a member of support staff, I want a record of whether each message was sent, delivered or failed on each channel, linked to the order or shipment, so that I can prove customers were notified and fix failed messages.
As a client administrator, I want delivery reports by channel and event type, so that I can see which channels work.
As a shopper, I want a bell icon in my account with my recent notifications and an unread count, so that I can see past messages in one place.

As a member of support staff, I want to send a message to a chosen group of affected customers, for example everyone whose parcel is delayed at one hub, so that customers hear about problems before they complain.
As a member of support staff, I want a banner on the site and the tracking page when a service is disrupted or tracking updates are delayed, so that customers know updates may be late.
As a seller, I want to see when my parcels were handed over and delivered, so that I can answer my own customers.
As a seller, I want to see the full tracking timeline of my shipments, so that I can follow problem parcels.
As a guest shopper, I want to check my order status with the order number and my phone number or email, without logging in, so that I can track an order placed as a guest.
As a shopper, I want messages when my parcel is shipped, out for delivery, ready for pickup and delivered, on the channels I use, so that I always know what is happening.
As a shopper, I want the pickup message to say where, when and what to bring, so that I can collect without a wasted trip.
As a shopper, I want to be told when a delivery attempt failed, why, and how to reschedule, so that I can arrange another attempt.
As a shopper, I want reminders before the pickup deadline and a notice when my parcel is still uncollected, so that I do not lose my parcel.
